terms.definition: A chemical carried in the blood that affects target organs; produced by a gland of the endocrine system.
terms.examiner: Hormonal effects are slower but longer lasting than nervous ones.

terms.definition: The "master gland" in the brain that secretes several hormones, some of which stimulate other glands.
terms.examiner: It releases ADH, FSH, LH and TSH.

terms.definition: A hormone from the pancreas that causes glucose to move from the blood into cells; in liver and muscle, glucose is converted to glycogen for storage.
terms.examiner: Released when blood glucose is too high.

terms.definition: A hormone from the pancreas that causes glycogen to be converted to glucose and released into the blood.
terms.examiner: Higher tier. Released when blood glucose is too low.

terms.definition: The pancreas does not make enough insulin, so blood glucose can rise uncontrollably; treated with insulin injections.
Body cells no longer respond to insulin; treated with a carbohydrate-controlled diet and exercise.
When a level changes from normal, a response brings it back to normal.
terms.examiner: Higher tier: the level of thyroxine is controlled by negative feedback.
